fault_reaction.allocation_basis: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001.fault_reaction entry 1 ('Open all high-voltage contactors, disable charging, latch the fault and log it', element_id AR-004, reaction_time_budget_ms 35). The same element and budget appear in FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.fault_reaction, which adds that the reaction is realised by FB2-SW-SWR-000003 in software and FB2-HW-TSR-000003 in hardware and that the watchdog that makes it work after a software hang is independent of the main microcontroller (FB2-ASM-007). The five segments come from FB2-SAF-SGO-000001.timing_budget.allocation: contactor_command_ms 5, contactor_mechanical_ms 30, feedback_verification_ms 5, with sys_state_transition_ms 3 in front of them. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000024 is the record in which three figures for one chain were reconciled and this element's 35 ms was separated from the 40 ms end-to-end figure.
fault_reaction.mode_dependence: Mode-dependent, and this is the load-bearing caveat of the concept. In MOD-004, with the contactors closed and current flowing, opening them removes propulsion from a moving vehicle, so the item must distinguish a genuine limit violation from a degraded condition and must not enter FAULT for the latter. In MOD-001, MOD-002 and MOD-007 the reaction is unambiguous and immediate; in MOD-006 the state is already latched. Disconnecting a battery is itself an action with consequences and is not unconditionally safe, which is why FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 states the situation-dependence rather than assuming it away. This requirement's conditions_modes includes FAULT, so the modes from which the reaction may be entered and the conditions under which the state machine may be driven into it are named; which of them actually applies is the state machine's decision and not this requirement's.
fault_reaction.open_limits: Three limits are recorded and none is closed by this field. First, this record states a 50 ms weld-detection latency and FB2-HW-TSR-000003 states 100 ms for the same quantity. No record in this corpus decides which is intended, so neither figure was changed and the disagreement was left open rather than harmonised by editing one of the two numbers; FB2-REV-FND-000024 records it as deliberately not resolved. Second, FB2-ASM-007 assumes the safe base controller's watchdog is independent of the main microcontroller and can actuate the contactors on its own; FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.hardware_interfaces_and_assumptions records that this independence is read out of the source and that its behaviour over the full supply and temperature range is not measured, and that if it does not hold, a software hang leaves the contactors in their last commanded state with AR-005 the only remaining path. Third, the 35 ms and 40 ms figures are allocations of intent; at the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005 the chain is 5 + 40 + 5 = 50 ms, and the corpus contains no worst-case analysis, no WCET and no measured execution time for any segment of it.
fault_reaction.reaction: De-energise every HV contactor coil through the safe base controller, confirm the commanded state from the auxiliary feedback, latch the fault and log it. This is the reaction FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 allocates to AR-004, and it is the only reaction on the main path that actually reaches the safe state. Both concepts give it 35 ms, which is the coil command at 5 ms plus the mechanical opening at 30 ms from FB2-PRM-000005; the confirmation of the commanded state is a further 5 ms that neither concept's 35 ms figure includes. Measured from the FAULT request the reaction is therefore complete at 40 ms, which is the figure this requirement's own acceptance criteria now ask for and the figure FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 allocates. If the commanded state is not confirmed by the feedback, the reaction does not fail silently: the disagreement between command and feedback is itself a diagnosis entry, and the opening is re-attempted rather than abandoned.
fault_reaction.reaction_completeness_note: 35 ms and 40 ms are not two answers to the same question. 35 ms is the mechanically open point, being contactor_command 5 ms plus contactor_mechanical 30 ms. 40 ms adds the feedback_verification 5 ms and is the point at which the safe state is CONFIRMED rather than merely commanded. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 both record 35 ms as the reaction budget and both compute the 40 ms end-to-end figure in their timing material; FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.ftti_and_timing_budget.arithmetic_check states the chain as 5 + 30 + 5 = 40 ms explicitly. The 30 ms mechanical figure is FB2-PRM-000005 (contactor_mechanical_time_ms = 30, tolerance 20..40) and FB2-ASM-006, and it is not what this element's 35 ms is made of on its own.
fault_reaction.triggered_by: A FAULT state request from the SOA monitor (FB2-SAF-FSR-000002) or from a diagnosis entry; and, independently of that request, any state of the auxiliary feedback that disagrees with the commanded state, which is the weld-detection path.

record_verbatim.rationale: Contactor opening is the primary risk reduction measure. The chain is three segments, and each segment has its own bound: the coil command within 5 ms, the mechanical opening within 30 ms (FB2-PRM-000005, FB2-ASM-006, worst case over -40 to +85 degC), and the auxiliary feedback confirmation within a further 5 ms. From the FAULT request the mechanically open point is therefore 5 + 30 = 35 ms and the feedback-confirmed point is 5 + 30 + 5 = 40 ms, which is the same 40 ms the safety goal allocates (contactor_command 5 + contactor_mechanical 30 + feedback_verification 5) and which fits inside the 100 ms fault-tolerant time interval with the 15 ms margin FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 now records. The earlier wording of this record stated a 30 ms threshold against a 35 ms rationale, which contradicted its own 5 ms coil-command criterion and the safety goal's 40 ms; the three figures were true of three different points on one chain and the defect was that a single criterion carried the value belonging to another point. Finding FB2-REV-FND-000024.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Reconciled the contactor reaction figures, which gave three different numbers for one chain: a 30 ms acceptance threshold, 35 ms in this record's own rationale and 40 ms in the safety goal's timing budget. Root cause was that 30 ms is the mechanical opening time alone - the value of FB2-PRM-000005 and FB2-ASM-006 - while the acceptance criterion it was attached to measures from the FAULT request to the FEEDBACK-open contactor, which additionally includes the coil command and the feedback confirmation. The chain was allocated in the safety goal as contactor_command 5 ms + contactor_mechanical 30 ms + feedback_verification 5 ms = 40 ms, and both the functional and the technical safety concept independently state that 40 ms is the end-to-end figure. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000024. Changes: (1) the 'Contactor open latency' threshold moves from 30 ms to 40 ms, because that criterion measures FAULT request to feedback open and 40 ms is what the allocated chain costs; (2) a new criterion 'Contactor mechanically open latency' is added at 35 ms for the FAULT request to mechanically open point, so the 30 ms mechanical parameter is no longer asked for under the wrong label; (3) the statement now distinguishes the mechanically open point (35 ms) from the feedback-confirmed point (40 ms); (4) the rationale is rewritten to state the full chain 5 + 30 + 5 = 40 ms and to say why the earlier 35 ms omitted the coil command. The coil de-energise criterion at 5 ms, the feedback-verification criterion and the weld-detection criterion are unchanged. No threshold was loosened to make a test pass: the 40 ms figure is the budget the record was already spending from, and adopting it makes the requirement harder to claim compliance with, not easier. The real foxBMS source was checked first and cannot settle the number - CONT_OpenContactor at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:165-182 requests the state change through SPS_RequestContactorState() and carries no timing constant - so the parameter registry FB2-PRM-000005 is the authority and it was not edited.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the fault_reaction this requirement was missing. AR-004 is the element the synthetic_reference copy of this requirement was already being measured against and is the only element on the main path that reaches the safe state, so the reaction is the one FB2-SAF-FSC-000001.fault_reaction entry 1 already allocates: open all high-voltage contactors, disable charging, latch the fault and log it, at 35 ms. The field records explicitly why 35 and 40 are not in conflict - 35 ms is the mechanically open point (command 5 ms plus mechanical 30 ms from FB2-PRM-000005) and 40 ms adds the 5 ms feedback_verification and is the point at which the safe state is confirmed rather than merely commanded, which is the same distinction FB2-REV-FND-000024 drew when it reconciled this record's three figures. It is carried in its own field rather than folded into the number so that a later reader cannot reintroduce the same confusion. mode_dependence reproduces the FSC's load-bearing caveat rather than assuming the reaction is unconditionally safe. open_limits carries forward the two things FB2-REV-FND-000024 deliberately left open - the 50 ms against 100 ms weld-detection disagreement with FB2-HW-TSR-000003, which was not harmonised by editing either number, and the unmeasured watchdog independence of FB2-ASM-007 - and adds the tolerance case: at the 40 ms upper tolerance of FB2-PRM-000005 the chain is 50 ms, and no worst-case analysis exists. Revision 2 -> 3. Statement, rationale, all six acceptance criteria including the three that FB2-REV-FND-000024 introduced, safety_allocation, the ASIL and the safety goal reference are unchanged and no threshold was relaxed. Human approval remains pending, production_authorized stays false and product_verification_credit stays false.

safety_allocation.mitigation: Feedback monitoring, independent SBC watchdog, weld detection, redundant contactors
